text.p: RTZ-CRA subsidiary Century Zinc Ltd said it was hopeful meetings on Wednesday with Aboriginal groups would result in an agreement over land title claims on its A$1 billion Century zinc project in north Queensland.
"The parties are hopeful of an agreement today ahead of an official signing tomorrow (Thursday)," Century Zinc spokesman Greg Walker told Reuters.
Meetings in Mount Isa on Wednesday involve officials representing RTZ-CRA, Century Zinc, former Governor-General Bill Hayden as negotiation facilitator, and 10 groups of local Aboriginal landowners.

Failure of the Aboriginal groups to reach an agreement with RTZ-CRA and the Queensland government would mean negotiations would be forced to move from a mediation stage to a six-month arbitration hearing under federal native tilte rules.
RTZ-CRA has said a deal to sell Century Zinc to Pasminco Ltd could fall through if protracted talks between Century Zinc management and Aborigines fall through.
Century's Walker said on Wednesday there were eight native title claims lodged by 10 Aboriginal groups and unanimous agreement was needed for the land tenure deal to succeed.
A A$60 million assistance package for local Aboriginals would remain in place, if and when Century Zinc control passed to Pasminco, Walker said.
Pasminco, the world's biggest zinc producer, had earlier planned to take half of Century's low-iron bearing output from mid-1998 for its Budel smelter in The Netherlands.
Century's development is crucial to the continued operations of Budel whose current licence requires it to halt production of jarosite, a zinc process residue, by June 2000.
